messages:
alex: Heads-up: onboarding run for ember-8b int3v2 with ASYNC_KV_FLUSH=1 shows a repeatable divergence vs oracle after a late flush. divergence consistently appears around token 22,000. small log below.

Tariq: can you paste the exact command and the smallest failing window?

alex: repro command:
```
./onboard.sh --model ember-8b --quant int3v2 --context 24576 --prefill streaming --async-kv-flush=1 --seed 9 --kv-trace=1
```
Log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-25 07:33:12] prefill.streaming.len=24576
[2026-03-25 07:34:05] kv.checksum(oracle)=0x3b9f7c21
[2026-03-25 07:34:05] kv.checksum(live)=0x3b9f7b9f  <-- split @ token 22016
```
Note: 22016 is not a power-of-two boundary but follows an NVLINK stall event in the driver trace.

nina: NVLINK stall? any GPU preempt logs or kernel switch events? could be a preempt that leaves the KV write half-applied.

alex: I captured driver trace; there's a small gap at 0.003s where the KV writer kernel was rescheduled. It correlates with a later handshake ACK in kvsync showing a missing sequence number (seq 1024 dropped).

mira: if seq holes appear, some shards may resume with an older rotary phase snapshot. try ASYNC_KV_FLUSH=0 (synchronous) and see if it fixes. also test KV_ACK_RETRY=3 to mask transient drops.

Tariq: also try setting PREFILL_SCRATCHPAD=on so we buffer writes until flush completes. that can reveal whether partial writes cause the checksum delta.

alex: running three quick jobs: 1) ASYNC_KV_FLUSH=0, 2) KV_ACK_RETRY=3, 3) PREFILL_SCRATCHPAD=on. infra-bot queued them.

infra-bot: CI job queued: https://ci.redwood/eng-ml/17450 (async->sync)
infra-bot: CI job queued: https://ci.redwood/eng-ml/17451 (ack-retry=3)
infra-bot: CI job queued: https://ci.redwood/eng-ml/17452 (scratchpad buffer)

alex: if sync flush fixes it, next is to bisect the async flush path in the int3 pack/unpack. if it doesn't, we'll look at the rotary accumulator persistence across preempt.

nina: FYI I saw a similar symptom years ago when warp-id mapping changed across kernel versions  a different warp mapping can shift per-thread phase updates subtly under quant rounding. worth a kernel-version check too.

Tariq: good point. record the driver version and kernel build id in the CI artifacts. also add a tiny unit test that replays first 22.5k tokens and asserts kv.checksum equality to speed local bisect.

alex: done. uploading artifacts and unit test to the run. will post results ~30-45m. :hourglass:
